title: Licensed Practical and Licensed Vocational Nurses
description: Care for ill, injured, or convalescing patients or persons with disabilities in hospitals, nursing homes, clinics, private homes, group homes, and similar institutions. May work under the supervision of a registered nurse. Licensing required.

tasks.text: Provide basic patient care or treatments, such as taking temperatures or blood pressures, dressing wounds, treating bedsores, giving enemas or douches, rubbing with alcohol, massaging, or performing catheterizations.

Provide medical treatment or personal care to patients in private home settings, such as cooking, keeping rooms orderly, seeing that patients are comfortable and in good spirits, or instructing family members in simple nursing tasks.
Help patients with bathing, dressing, maintaining personal hygiene, moving in bed, or standing and walking.
Apply compresses, ice bags, or hot water bottles.
Wash and dress bodies of deceased persons.
Measure and record patients' vital signs, such as height, weight, temperature, blood pressure, pulse, or respiration.
Collect samples, such as blood, urine, or sputum from patients, and perform routine laboratory tests on samples.
Administer prescribed medications or start intravenous fluids, noting times and amounts on patients' charts.
Record food and fluid intake and output.
Supervise nurses' aides or assistants.
Prepare or examine food trays for conformance to prescribed diet.
Assemble and use equipment, such as catheters, tracheotomy tubes, or oxygen suppliers.
Set up equipment and prepare medical treatment rooms.
Sterilize equipment and supplies, using germicides, sterilizer, or autoclave.
Clean rooms and make beds.
Observe patients, charting and reporting changes in patients' conditions, such as adverse reactions to medication or treatment, and taking any necessary action.
Answer patients' calls and determine how to assist them.
Evaluate nursing intervention outcomes, conferring with other healthcare team members as necessary.
Work as part of a healthcare team to assess patient needs, plan and modify care, and implement interventions.
Make appointments, keep records, or perform other clerical duties in doctors' offices or clinics.
Prepare patients for examinations, tests, or treatments and explain procedures.
Inventory and requisition supplies and instruments.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Mathematics
skills.def: Using mathematics to solve problems.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Negotiation
skills.def: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Medical software
skills.def: Software to evaluate, plan, or redesign healthcare procedures. May include reporting or visualization features. Examples: eClinicalWorks EHR software, Electronic medical record EMR software, Epic Systems, Healthcare common procedure coding system HCPCS.

skills.name: Video conferencing software
skills.def: Software to enable audio or video conferences between participants using networked devices. Examples: FaceTime, Zoom.

skills.name: Electronic mail software
skills.def: Software to compose, send, or receive email. Examples: Microsoft Exchange, Microsoft Outlook.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Operating system software
skills.def: Software to provide the operational interface to a computer and provide higher-level services and APIs. Examples: Microsoft Windows.
